SK·09·LIS

Shingō

信号
2026

An industrial interface system for iOS and the web. Interfaces are printed on a striped ground: hard 45° cuts, hazard bars, chevrons, barcodes and mono telemetry, with one coral signal per screen. English leads, with Japanese and français woven in sparingly.

darkink ground, bone print
lightsage ground, ink print

Every screen ships in both modes with the same layering. Dark prints bone on ink stripes. Light prints ink on the poster's sage, with paper plates that are never white. Coral is the same in both. The page follows your system setting, and the switch in the corner flips it.

Key art

both references merged: the print stack of the shirt, the instrument column of the poster
Shape alphabet12 primitives · one angle (45°, rising "/") · flat print · no rounding
A · Cut plate

Chamfers at top-left and bottom-right only, at 6, 12 or 24 pt. Buttons, keys, cards.

B · Tag

One cut, bottom-right. The coral signal slab and every bar's free end.

C · Nested bar

Print, ground, print, slot. The hero form, progress and scrubber.

D · Slash

A "/" parallelogram. Steps, cells and stripes are all slashes in a row.

E · Hazard

Slashes between two rules. The divider between masthead and body.

F · Notch

A hairline frame with its label tab cut into the corner, like a drawing's title block.

G · Hard X

Two crossed bars, square-cut ends. Solid for done, outline for rest, coral for now.

H · Diamond

A square turned 45° with an off-centre hole. The mark, blips and bullets.

I · Chevrons

Nested "^" with broken left arms. The one large artwork: hero, key art, paywall.

J · Brackets

Four L corners around anything that is a viewport: scopes, spectra, faces.

K · Cell run

Slashes that fill up. Levels, rounds and caps.

L · Wedge

A 45° triangle of coral in a corner. Poster screens only.

02

Screens

iPhone 390 × 844 pt · one grammar, two tiers · placeholder brand "AXIOM"
01Two inks

Everything is print on ground: solid shapes in the print ink with text knocked out, or outlines. No third tone. Coral is the only extra ink.

02One grammar

Masthead, one hero, a divider, the body, the imprint. Each screen sits on one backdrop composition from the shape alphabet. Poster screens compose freely.

03One angle

Every diagonal rises left to right at 45°: corner cuts (top-left and bottom-right), hazard stripes, cells, bands and the stripe field. No tilts, textures or shadows.

04Three sizes

Wordmark type at 44 for display, 26 for titles and 15 inline. Labels are condensed caps and telemetry is mono.

05One signal

Coral marks one block or one primary action per screen, plus the latest or active state. Switches turn on in print, not coral.

06Tag and aside

Japanese lives in the masthead tag or a seal. French lives in the span rule. Each appears once at most.

Instruments

useful, decorative parts extrapolated from the system · every one is live

Seven-segment readoutseg7() · SGSegDisplay

Big numerals for timers, speed, balances and counters, in thin upright segments. Any digit can light coral.

Cell meter.cells · SGCellMeter

Cells slanted at the system's 45°, like a hazard stripe that fills up. For levels, rounds and caps. The last cell can run hot.

Ruler slider.ruler · SGRuler

A tick scale with a coral needle for volume, zoom, temperature or intensity. Drag it.

020406080100

Slash steps.steps · SGSteps

A process printed as "/" plates, the system's one diagonal: done in print, current in coral, upcoming in ground-3. For onboarding, checkout and setup.

Index tabs.itabs · SGIndexTabs

Manual-divider tabs on a print rule. A sturdier alternative to the segmented control for page-level sections.

A hairline frame whose label tab is cut into its corner, like the title block on an engineering drawing. For tiles and grouped readouts.

Three languages

english · 日本語 · français
EN

English runs the interface

Every action, label and number. If someone has to read it to use the app, it's in English.

Protected
日本語

Japanese adds texture

Vertical captions along edges, seal stamps and outlined display kanji. Use one Japanese moment per screen at most. It is never the only label on a control.

認証受信箱圏外
Fr.

French is the aside

Italic footnotes, dates, taglines and pull quotes. Use it once per screen at most, usually in the quietest spot.

« celui qu'on n'entend pas »
×3

All three only once

Stack the same line in all three languages in one place only: the lock screen, splash or about page. Repeating the stack elsewhere weakens it.

07

Origins

reference 1, the sage and coral poster, rebuilt from primitives

Reference 1 gave Shingō its palette: sage, ink and coral, the striped ground, the nested forms and the right-aligned telemetry.

Reference 2, a trilingual technical print, gave it its voice: wide industrial type, hazard bars, chevrons, barcodes and the line-art head. It also brought English with Japanese and French woven in.

Shingō now leans toward the second reference. Pills became cut bars, rounded X marks became hard ones, and soft panels gave way to print. The poster stays here as the source of the color and the layering.
